chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Kid Ory's Creole Trombone, Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper and the Sunshine label
summary: Spikes says he was only the promoter, that Ory's band was called Kid Ory's Creole Band and had to paste his Sunshine labels over Nordskog's name.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And that band was called, uh, Reb Spikes' or the Spikes Brothers'? The Spikes Brothers...
No, it was called "Kid Ory's Creole Trombone" but I had a band at the time called "Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper," and they got it all mixed up.
Oh. 'Cause I understood from what I read that Kid Ory was on the record but the...it was...you...you were the leader, and it was under the name of your band.

No, I was just the promoter. Kid Ory... I had the music store, and I wanted some records by Kid Ory because he was very popular, and he made the records, and it is Kid Ory's band but they called it the uh, I think, the...some of the records had on it "Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper" but my other band...I had another little band that I called Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper. His was called the Kid Ory's Creole Band.
I see, and that was what was supposed to be on the record.
Yeah. Yeah. But he recorded it for Spikes' Record Company.
I see. And there was one...I think it was one of these magazines showed two different labels--this one, the Storyville, and Sunshine...
It shows Ruth Lee on there. And Nordskog--Ory's
Creole Trombones, Spikes' Seven Pods of Pepper.

Well, you see, that's what I'm...told you--that he put his label on them, and I had to put my own label over the top of them. See, I had to glue mine on. When you make a record, you know, you put it in the machine with it, and the machine presses it right into the matrix. See? Now you get a big...they'll...they put a ball of--that matrix is a ball like that, and they stick it under the machine, and when the machine come down, it presses it out. But you stick your label in there first. Then when the ends come together to cut through the hole through there, they press the label right on there. You don't have to seal it. 'Cause this is hot, and...uh...but he put those on when he had 'em pressed. Then when I come to my store, I put my labels...had my labels there, and I had to just paste them over the top of these, 'cause they wasn't a Nordskog Record; they was Spikes...uh, Sunshine Records.
